title: A document that stops existing the moment the person is forgotten
summary: Files are encrypted per person, not per system: the key that unwraps a person's documents is one database row. Erasure deletes that row, and every document of that person becomes unreadable at commit time - no storage round trip, no cleanup job to trust.

steps.label: The person whose document this is
steps.note: Every file hangs off a pseudonym, never off a name or an identifier.

steps.label: Listing without a stated purpose is refused
steps.note: Metadata IS disclosure - a filename like 'otkaz-2026.pdf' says plenty. So listing carries the same purpose and consent gate as reading the content, and it is audited the same way.

steps.label: With a purpose, the list is empty
steps.note: Nothing stored yet. Note that the empty answer is still an audited read: 'who looked' is recorded even when there was nothing to see.

steps.label: The person withdraws consent for support
steps.note: Before uploading anything, watch consent govern the file surface too - the same decision that blocks an attribute read blocks the documents.

steps.label: Listing is now refused
steps.note: Consent is enforced at the vault, not in the calling application. Nothing about the caller changed.

steps.label: Consent restored
steps.note: Withdrawal is reversible and both decisions stay on the record.

steps.label: Erase the person
steps.note: This is the step the whole feature exists for. Erasure deletes the person's record key - the one row that unwraps every per-file key they have. Their documents do not need to be found and deleted; they become undecryptable in the same transaction.

steps.label: The document surface is gone with them
steps.note: The pseudonym still resolves to a tombstone - client references never break - but there is nothing left to list, and no key left to read anything with.
